summary: TWT Phase 2 (Stops + Attractions + Drag&Drop) full-stack testing. Backend: new suite /app/backend/tests/phase2_test.py (46 tests) + Phase 1 regression (23 tests) => 69 passed, 2 xfail (documented defects). Covered: member gating on stops list (200/401/404), stop create with auto order max+1 and all field echo, all stop validations (end<start, dates outside trip range with range in message, invalid transport_mode, negative km, 25:00 time, empty title), PATCH partial + effective-range revalidation on start_date-only update (422 + no mutation), DELETE stop 204 with attraction cascade verified in Mongo, stops /reorder (order=index, response sorted, unknown id -> 422), attractions list/create (currency defaults to trip.home_currency, currency lowercased normalized to USD, order auto max+1), attraction validations (cost/duration>=0, currency enum, scheduled_time HH:mm, empty name), PATCH all fields + GET persistence, DELETE 204/404, attractions /reorder same-stop reorder, cross-stop move in one atomic call, and atomic rollback verified directly in Mongo for unknown attraction_id and unknown target_stop_id (DB byte-identical before/after), negative new_order and empty moves -> 422, viewer-role matrix (GET 200; POST/PATCH/DELETE/reorder on stops+attractions all 403) using a directly-seeded trip_members viewer row for bob@twt.app, /api/openapi.json 200 and lists all 6 new paths. Frontend (Playwright on public preview URL, dev-login cookie): dashboard regression (3 trips listed, trip creation via UI+API OK), /trip/{id} sticky sub-header (title, Sep 1 2030 -> Sep 30 2030, OWNER badge, 'KM total: —' 'Spend total: —'), empty state 'Draw your route.' + empty-stops-create-btn, stop create via both CTAs (number bubble, transport icon PLANE/CAR, location, date chip), date inputs bound min=2030-09-01/max=2030-09-30, modal client validation (end<start -> stop-modal-error), attraction create x3 (default currency EUR shown, amber cost badge rgb(245,184,65) '€10.00', link target=_blank), same-stop DRAG reorder (A1,A2,A3 -> A2,A3,A1) persisted after reload, cross-stop DRAG from Lisbon drop zone to Porto drop zone persisted after reload, optimistic-UI rollback verified by stubbing POST /attractions/reorder with 500 (list reverted + toast 'Reorder failed — reverted'), attraction edit (name+cost persisted after reload), attraction delete confirm dialog -> removed, stop three-dot menu edit (title updated) and delete dialog -> stop + its attractions removed (backend list confirms), viewer role UI (badge 'viewer', zero add-stop/add-attraction/stop-menu/drag-handle controls, attractions still readable). 2 backend defects found (trip delete does not cascade stops/attractions; stops reorder accepts a subset of stop_ids producing duplicate order values).

critical.issue: No cascade delete of stops/attractions. Deleting a trip leaves orphaned stops+attractions in Mongo forever (35 orphan stops / 20 orphan attractions accumulated during this test run and had to be cleaned manually). trips.py delete_trip only deletes trip_members + trips.

minor.issue: Validation only checks that supplied stop_ids exist in the trip, not that they cover ALL trip stops. Posting a strict subset returns 200 and sets order=index, producing duplicate order values (observed [S0=0, S2=0, S1=1]) and a non-deterministic timeline order.

bulk_write is not a Mongo transaction; pre-validation makes the happy path safe, but a mid-flight failure (or a concurrent delete between validation and write) can still leave a partially applied reorder and returns 500 'Partial reorder failure'. Consider a session/transaction or an idempotent re-normalize step.
Explicit nulls are handled via model_fields_set, but km_from_prev/notes cannot be distinguished from 'unset' in some client payloads; low impact, no functional failure observed.

Remaining stops are not re-indexed after a delete, leaving order gaps (e.g. single remaining stop keeps order=1). UI renders index-based numbering so it is cosmetic today, but future order math should not assume contiguity.

issues: Stop connector chip always shows '– km' when km_from_prev is unset; a placeholder dash chip between every stop adds visual noise (consider hiding when null)
'KM total: —' / 'Spend total: —' remain dashes even after km_from_prev=120 is saved — expected per Phase 2 spec (placeholders), flagging so it is not mistaken for a regression later
Attraction edit/delete buttons only appear on hover with no focus-visible state — not reachable by keyboard-only users (same pattern as the Phase 1 trip delete button)

Start/End still use native <input type=date> instead of the shadcn Calendar (carried over from Phase 1). Out-of-trip-range dates are blocked silently by native HTML5 min/max constraint validation, so no in-app stop-modal-error is displayed — the user sees only the browser tooltip.

action_items: HIGH: add cascade delete of db.stops and db.attractions in trips.delete_trip (DELETE /api/trips/{trip_id}); orphans currently persist forever
Tighten POST /stops/reorder validation: require stop_ids to be a full permutation of the trip's stop_ids (set equality against ALL trip stops), else 422
Optional: re-normalize stop order after a stop delete so order stays contiguous
Optional: use a Mongo session/transaction for attractions bulk reorder to make partial-failure impossible
Optional UX: surface out-of-trip-range date errors in stop-modal-error instead of relying only on native min/max validation; add focus-visible states to hover-only attraction action buttons
critical_code_review_comments: trips.py delete_trip cascades trip_members but not stops/attractions — data-integrity leak confirmed against Mongo.
stops.reorder_stops compares existing_ids to set(body.stop_ids) only; a subset passes and creates duplicate order values.
attractions.reorder_attractions relies on pre-validation + bulk_write instead of a transaction; the 500 'Partial reorder failure' branch can leave inconsistent state.
Trip.jsx is 604 lines and holds fetch/DnD/modal/dialog state — close to the 700-line limit; consider extracting the DnD move-diff logic and the dialogs into hooks/components before Phase 3.
Attraction booking_link is a plain max_length=500 string (not HttpUrl) and is rendered into an <a href> — validate the scheme server-side to avoid javascript: URLs.

success_rate.backend: 100% of specified Phase 2 behaviours (69 passed / 2 xfail documented defects)
success_rate.frontend: 100% of tested flows (stops, attractions, same-stop + cross-stop drag persistence, rollback, edit/delete dialogs, viewer gating, fonts)

seed_data_creation: Trips/stops/attractions created with TEST_ prefix and deleted at the end. UI trip trip_e746f90dd00842a7 (TEST_UI_P2) deleted; its manually seeded viewer trip_members row for bob@twt.app removed. 35 orphan stops / 20 orphan attractions left behind by the non-cascading trip delete were cleaned manually — Mongo stops/attractions collections are now empty.
test_credentials: POST /api/auth/dev-login {email,name} (ENV=dev). alice@twt.app (owner), bob@twt.app (2nd user/viewer), carol@twt.app. Cookie twt_session (httpOnly, SameSite=None, Secure); body also returns session_token for Bearer.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run both suites: `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/ -q` (pytest.ini forces -n 2 --dist loadscope, so every test class must be self-sufficient — do NOT rely on state created by another class on a module-scoped fixture). phase2_test.py has 2 xfail(strict=False) tests in TestKnownDefects: they will flip to XPASS once trip-delete cascade and full-permutation reorder validation are implemented — convert them to plain asserts then. Frontend recipe that works: page.goto(BASE) -> page.evaluate(fetch('/api/auth/dev-login', {credentials:'include'})) -> goto /trip/{id}. Drag&drop works headless with manual mouse steps: mouse.move to attr-drag-{id} center, mouse.down, small 5px jiggle move, then move in ~25 steps to the target (attraction-item-{id} for same-stop, stop-drop-zone-{stop_id} for cross-stop), pause 400ms, mouse.up. Viewer UI can be simulated by upserting a trip_members {role:'viewer',status:'accepted'} row for bob's user_id.
rca_of_the_issue: Orphan data: delete_trip in /app/backend/trips.py deletes only trip_members and trips; stops.delete_stop implements attraction cascade but nothing cascades from the trip level, so every trip deletion leaks all of its stops and attractions (reproduced: create trip -> stop -> attraction -> DELETE /api/trips/{id} -> Mongo still has 1 stop + 1 attraction). Reorder gap: stops.reorder_stops validates only that each supplied stop_id exists in the trip (existing_ids == set(body.stop_ids)), which is trivially true for any subset, so order=index assignment collides with the untouched stops' existing order values.
